newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by ongoing weak pork demand and poor packer operating margins, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant could range $49.00 to $49.50.
Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $49.50 to $50.50, they said. Indidana/Ohio top plant prices for hogs could range $49.50 to $50.50.
The weak pork demand was offsetting potential support from lighter marketings, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Tuesday totalled 98,000 head, USDA said. Tuesday's estimate was 105,000. Wednesday's estimate was 95,000 head.
The top price for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs Wednesday was $50.50, down $3.00 per cwt from a week ago, USDA statistics showed.
Pork prices were expected lower by Wednesday's close, which could further weaken outlooks for cash hog prices on Thursday, the dealers said.
At midday, fresh loins were not fully established, butts were mostly $1.00 per cwt lower, hams were steady to $2.00 lower and pork bellies were steady, USDA said.
